messages.author: e4231721a931f6e2
messages.subject: Tokens
parts:
Contrary to what Günter said, I rather like the ShinyApp setup here. In about twenty minutes, I was able to take one of the apps I was running locally and upload it to the server for my boss and her clients to see some 3000 miles away. The only confusing part to me was that the dataset needed to be in the shiny folder instead of my project workspace, but once that was figured out, everything worked. Sweet!

I have another app that I am not yet ready to upload (waiting on permission to release the data), will I need another token to run both of these apps simultaneously? If not, what is the purpose of tokens?

Thanks,
Steve

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: Tokens
parts:
Steve,

Thanks for the kind words. We're glad you were able to get your app up and running so easily. That is our goal!

As for the tokens, their purpose is kind of like a username and password. You can deploy any number of apps using the same token. I would just recommend creating a new RStudio project/directory for each app.

Regards,
-Andy
